name: Finnhorse
notes: The Suomenhevonen - Finland's only native horse, and its national one. A northern farm-and-harness horse rather than a continental warmblood: forestry, fields, sleighs, cavalry, and now harness trotting.

Chestnut with a flaxen mane and tail is the breed, and it is a policy outcome rather than an ancient trait. The studbook closed in 1907 and twentieth-century policy refused colours it called foreign - grey, palomino, piebald, white - driving chestnut past 90% of the modern population. Flaxen is near-fixed on top of it.

The old diversity was not wholly erased, and this is the rare pool where the heritage minorities are the interesting part: bay at about 6% and black at about 1.2% (2007 figures), plus surviving traces of grey, cream, silver, dun, roan, rabicano and splash white 1, each at a percent or two.
Tobiano sits at four founders in a thousand. A single historical pinto is on record and piebalds were actively selected against; this preserves the outlier without creating a pinto population.

Sabino 1 is deliberately absent even though the breed has a moderately common minimally-expressed sabino-like pattern. That pattern is documented as non-SB1, so naming the mod's SB1 would assert a molecular result nobody has shown.

The four official sections since 1971 - trotter, riding, pony-sized, working - are NOT strains here. They are performance and inspection categories over one shared gene pool, earned individually and not inherited, so encoding them would invent four closed sub-breeds that do not exist. The size band spans them; only the pony section has a hard limit (148 cm) and only the general average (155-156 cm) is otherwise pinned.
Cold tolerant near-fixed, for Finnish winters, bogs and forest.
Flaxen's architecture is still incompletely resolved in the literature, so the near-fixed rate here is a gameplay reading of a visual hallmark, not a molecular frequency.

All disorders clear. The breed has real population-genetic concerns - one analysis put nuclear effective population near 50 per section against high mitochondrial variation - but a bottleneck is not a disease rate.
Uncommon rather than rare: the draft asked for rare, but this is a living national breed in regular harness use, not a remnant.
The trotting gait, the modest feathering and the thick mane and tail are none of them modelled.
